summary: Anderson Hollow light, first shown from a breakwater at Waterside in 1889; its 1903 shore tower, moved several times, is now a static display at Harvey Bank.

structures.note: Shore tower north of the government breakwater at Waterside, 31 ft to the vane. The 1903 report describes a square wooden lantern; the Lighthouse Directory describes no lantern and a non-working gallery. Now at Harvey Bank.

access.note: Site open, tower closed. Static display: visitors can look but not go inside.

facts.agency: Chipoudy Communities Revitalization Committee (owner since 2024; older listings name the Albert County Heritage Trust)

events.note: Beacon light at Anderson's Hollow, Chignecto Channel, first shown 1 August 1889, on the breakwater at Waterside (1889 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Heavy storm damaged the first tower (LighthouseFriends only)
Tower torn from its foundation, survived, returned to the wharf (LighthouseFriends only)
Gale of 21 November 1895 carried away the end of the pier and the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends only)
New enclosed tower on the outer end of the repaired public wharf; contract to H. O. Barbour for $182 (LighthouseFriends only)
Breakwater tower destroyed by storm 12 January 1902; a temporary mast light followed
Shore tower built north of the breakwater; first shown at the opening of navigation in 1903
Light established on the outer end of the government breakwater on a 22 ft pole. This is a breakwater mast light, not the shore tower.
Crib of stone built around the breakwater mast
Light formerly shown from the shore tower permanently discontinued (1909 report)
Moved to the Harvey Bank Heritage Shipyard Park, Mary's Point, on 31 October 2001 (LighthouseFriends)
Chipoudy Communities Revitalization Committee announced it had acquired the lighthouse and the Old Bank of New Brunswick

keepers.name: Rev. S. C. Moore

keepers.name: Ed. J. Copp
keepers.note: Given by LighthouseFriends only. The official name lists for 1901 and 1902 include 'Copp, Ed. J', but the OCR does not pair him with a station reliably.

keepers.name: Aaron B. Copp
keepers.note: Also written A. B. Copp. The 1903 keeper list pairs 'Copp, A. B' with Anderson Hollow. LighthouseFriends gives 1903 to 1911.

keepers.name: J. E. Moore
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives 1911 to at least 1923. Official keeper lists for 1912 to 1915 name a J. E. Moore, but the OCR does not pair him with this station.

corrections.why: The 1903 report describes the surviving shore tower as built and first shown at the opening of navigation in 1903. The 1907 entry in the 1907 report is a new light on the breakwater end, not this tower.
CCRC announced in a news item dated 4 June 2024 that it had acquired the lighthouse; the Lighthouse Directory and LighthouseFriends still name the Albert County Heritage Trust.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lighthouse Directory gives 1907 for the surviving tower. The 1903 report describes the shore tower as built and first shown in 1903, and the 1907 report describes a new mast light on the breakwater that year. LighthouseFriends also gives 1903.

1889 is the first light shown at Anderson's Hollow from the breakwater at Waterside (report as quoted by LighthouseFriends). The surviving tower is the 1903 shore tower. The record's coordinates are for the tower's present site at Harvey Bank, not the 1889 site.

notes_for_editor: The 1889 date and the 1889 quotations come only from LighthouseFriends quoting the 1889 report; the corpus does not hold 1889 and the story says so. The 1891, 1892, 1895 and 1898 events, the 1949 standby light, and the moves after 1909 (Herbert Armstrong's yard, the late-1980s Riverside-Albert site) come from LighthouseFriends alone; LighthouseFriends credits its move history to a local informant. Official reports in the corpus do not cover those years, so they are unchecked. Keeper evidence matched by position in the OCR, to check against the page images: Rev. S. C. Moore's appointment (14 May 1889) on the 1900 list (scan p. 225, printed p. 128), where his name, station and date sit on one OCR line; A. B. Copp's station is paired with Anderson Hollow in the 1903 list (scan p. 227, printed p. 214) by sequence in the OCR; Ed. J. Copp and J. E. Moore appear in official name lists without a station that I could pair reliably, so they rest on LighthouseFriends. Check the 1903 keeper list page image before relying on the A. B. Copp pairing. A W. C. Anderson appears in a 1909 wharfinger table for Anderson's Hollow (appointed 13 February 1899); he is not a keeper and is not linked to the W. C. Anderson LighthouseFriends names as builder of the 1903 tower. Rowlett gives 1907 for the tower; read as the 1907 breakwater mast light, which the 1907 report records. Rowlett describes no lantern while the 1903 report describes a square wooden lantern; unresolved. The record's coordinates are for the Harvey Bank site (LighthouseFriends gives 45.73518, -64.69728); the Waterside breakwater site has no coordinates in the sources read. The CCRC news item is dated 4/6/2024; read here as 4 June 2024 because it mentions June events. The CCRC move plan is dated 28 December 2025; the sources read do not say whether the move has happened. The 1903 range distance 'six miles' is printed without a unit qualifier; kept as printed. Private individuals (the 1980s owners of the Waterside house, the informant) are not named. Herbert Armstrong is named only as LighthouseFriends names him (a keeper at Martin Head in the early twentieth century). Not read: Wikidata, Wikimedia Commons, ARLHS CAN-704, Lighthouse Digest database entry. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the page images were read on archive.org for both keeper rows. The Moore row (scan 225, printed p. 128) and the Copp row (scan 227, printed p. 214) each read on one row, name, station and date together, as the OCR gives them; the images were read at low resolution, so the dates are as printed in the OCR.
